title: ZPA admin and RBAC audit: admins, roles, admin SSO, API keys, emergency access, microtenants, provisioning keys, PRA credentials and approvals

checks.what: every new ZPA read resolves to the installed SDK 1.11.3 base and path (PRA credential pools on waap-pra-config, admin SSO under /v2)
RBAC.13 to RBAC.23: pass, review, fail and N/A cases per check, with an injected clock
no key, password, secret, token or provisioning-key value and no admin name or e-mail in any result or its plain text
HTTP 403 is not permitted and not judged; 404 is not licensed / N/A
at most 10 pages per list and 20 per-microtenant reads
the new lists are read only with RBAC (and ZPA) ticked, listed on the Scope page, captured scrubbed in snapshots and served by the sample tenant
the checks only call get(); no write path is added

findings.title: Snapshot scrub masked tokenExpiryTimeInSec (a token lifetime, not a secret), so a token-lifetime check could never judge a snapshot or the sample
findings.fix: A numeric value under a lifetime name (expiry/expiration/lifetime/validity in seconds) is kept; token text is still masked.

findings.title: ZPA path resolution could only build mgmtconfig paths: PRA credential pools (waap-pra-config) had no path and its customer id was not normalised in snapshots
findings.fix: _ZPA_MAP entries may name a service base; offline_tenant normalises the waap-pra-config customer segment too.

findings.title: The ZPA admin and RBAC area (admins, roles, admin SSO, API keys, emergency access, microtenants, provisioning keys, PRA credentials and approvals) was not read or assessed
findings.fix: Eleven read-only checks (RBAC.13 to RBAC.23) in the RBAC registry, scrubbed on read, with snapshot capture and sample data.
